source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:35 (the Ramah: 'this alone lacks the yod; every slaves-word in the Torah plene')
claim_en: THE ONE LEAN SLAVES-WORD: ועבדם ('flocks and herds, silver and gold, AND SLAVES...' — the servant reciting Abraham's wealth, 24:35) — UNIQUE in the Torah and written DEFECTIVE (no yod), while every other slaves-word runs plene (builder-asserted over the whole plene family): the inventory-boast goes lean exactly at the human line.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:39 ('אלי written defective — and our rabbis expounded it in Bereshit Rabbah 59: Eliezer had a daughter and sought to give her to Isaac'; Rashi cited; Yalkut Hosea 528; the Gur Aryeh's resolution)
claim_en: THE SERVANT'S SECRET HOPE: אלי ('PERHAPS the woman will not follow me' — the oath retold, 24:39) — written DEFECTIVE, no vav: the perhaps-word collapses into TO-ME, and the midrash reads Eliezer's daughter-wish in the dropped letter ('Canaan holds deceitful scales,' Hos 12:8 behind it). SNAPSHOT: the qubutz-pointed lean perhaps is UNIQUE in the whole DB (builder-asserted single token)...

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:39 (the plene control at the first telling)
claim_en: ...while at the FIRST telling, face to face with Abraham, the same servant's perhaps is written FULL (אולי, 24:5): the hope hides only in the retelling — the letter drops the vav exactly where the midrash drops the mask.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:27 ('the second — with chirik'; pair completion from the road-thanksgiving)
claim_en: ONE VOWEL NARROWS THE FAMILY, completed: at the retelling's thanksgiving the same consonants take CHIRIK — בת אחי אדני ('the daughter of my master's BROTHER,' singular, 24:48) against the tzere plural of 24:27: the road-prayer thanked the whole kin-house; the report names one man.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:53 ('ומגדנת — the dalet DAGESHED')
claim_en: ומגדנת ('and PRECIOUS THINGS to her brother and mother') — UNIQUE in the Torah, and the dalet carries dagesh as ruled: the gift-word appears once, dotted, at the bride-price.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:53 (the dagesh leg)
claim_en: ...the dot verified in the stream.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:55 ('one of the verses our rabbis called ITUR SOFERIM — the scribes' adornment — as I wrote at the end of Behaalotekha')
claim_en: THE SCRIBES' ADORNMENT, SECOND TORAH MEMBER: אחר תלך ('let the maiden stay... AFTERWARD she shall go,' 24:55) — written bare אחר with no joining vav, one of the itur soferim (the scribes' adornment-list of expected-but-omitted vavs); the corpus's first member stands at frozen 18:5 ('AFTERWARD you shall pass on'). SNAPSHOT: bare, as the list requires.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:60 ('ויברכו — the resh with SHEVA')
claim_en: DISCREPANCY, THIRD STATION: ויברכו ('and they BLESSED Rebecca') — Minchat Shai rules the resh with plain sheva; SNAPSHOT points HATAF PATACH (the compound half-vowel): the bless-word vocalization split now counts three stations in the codex line (12:3's career-law, 22:18's Aqedah blessing, and the bride's send-off). Watchlist.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:60 ('the Hilleli copy: וירש; the Jerusalem: ויירש with the Masorah-note UNIQUE-PLENE — and so the precise books and the Ramah: plene')
claim_en: ויירש ('may your seed INHERIT the gate of its haters') — SNAPSHOT writes it PLENE, both yods, with the Jerusalem copy, the precise books and the Ramah's whole-Torah rule (frozen G38-07/08/09: the one defective inherit-verb is the Aqedah's), against the Hilleli's lean reading — the manuscript split named, the codex side declared.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 24:60 (רבבה four in the Masorah; the two-chase-a-myriad and the myriad-of-the-field named to her)
claim_en: רבבה ('be thou mother to thousands of MYRIADS') — THREE tokens in the Torah: Rebecca's blessing (24:60), the two-chase-a-myriad (Lev 26:8), the how-should-one-chase-a-myriad (Deut 32:30); the Masorah's fourth is Ezekiel's myriad-as-the-field-growth (Ezek 16:7; edge) — the bride blessed into the war-arithmetic of her children.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 24:67 ('ויבאה — two in the Masorah, in the book of Genesis, written defective; its letters count TWENTY-FOUR — she was adorned with twenty-four adornments')
claim_en: THE TWO BROUGHT BRIDES: ויבאה ('and he BROUGHT HER into the tent of Sarah his mother') — exactly TWICE in the Torah, both in Genesis: God bringing the first woman to the first man ('and He BROUGHT HER to the man,' 2:22) and Isaac bringing Rebecca into his mother's tent (24:67) — the Torah's only two bride-deliveries, one written form. And the lean word's letters count 6+10+2+1+5 = TWENTY-FOUR: the Kitzur's twenty-four adornments riding the sum.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 24:67 (האהלה eight in the Masorah — the eight dwellings of the Presence)
claim_en: האהלה ('INTO THE TENT') — SIX tokens in the Torah: Sarah's tent at the annunciation (18:6), Rebecca's entry (24:67), Jethro's welcome (Exod 18:7), the tent of meeting twice (Exod 33:8-9), Eldad and Medad's hour (Num 11:26); the Kitzur's eight-list spans Tanakh toward the Presence's eight dwellings (edges) — the tent-word with the leading-heh gathers the Shekhinah-stations.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 24:67 ('ויאהבה — two in the Masorah: here and Amnon's; there love hung on a thing and lapsed; here it hung on nothing and stood')
claim_en: ויאהבה ('and he LOVED HER') — UNIQUE in the Torah: Isaac's love appears once in the letter; the Masorah's pair-leg is Amnon's collapsing love (II Sam 13:1; edge) — love hung on a thing lapses, Isaac's stood.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 24:7 ('מלאכו written TWICE — he asked for one angel on the going and one on the return')
claim_en: מלאכו ('He shall send HIS ANGEL before you') — exactly TWO tokens in the Torah, BOTH in this chapter: Abraham's promise for the going (24:7) and the servant's retelling for the return (24:40) — one angel out, one angel back, precisely the Kitzur's count.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 24:56 ('אל תאחרו אתי וה׳ — the final letters: ESCORT — for they escorted him')
claim_en: THE ESCORT IN THE FINALS: אל תאחרו אתי ויהוה ('do not DELAY me, since YHWH has prospered my way,' 24:56) — the four words close ל-ו-י-ה: the letters of לויה ('escort'), in order — the send-off written into the seams of the impatience-verse.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 24:58 ('עם האיש הזה — the final letters: MOSES — she went according to the law of Moses and Israel')
claim_en: MOSES IN THE CONSENT: התלכי עם האיש הזה ('will you GO with this man?') — the three question-closing words end ם-ש-ה: the letters of משה ('Moses'), in order — the Kitzur reads the bride's free consent as already under the law of Moses and Israel.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 24:47 ('ואשם — lacking the yod: he did not touch her flesh, not even with the yod of his fingers, out of modesty')
claim_en: ואשם ('and I PLACED the ring on her nose' — the retelling, 24:47) — written WITHOUT the yod (builder-asserted), and the Kitzur rides the missing letter: he placed without touching, 'not even with the yod of his fingers.'

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:3 ('the first: in whose MIDST I dwell; the second: in whose LAND — one verse their mnemonic: for I am YHWH in the midst of the land')
claim_en: THE OATH NARROWS IN THE RETELLING: Abraham swears the servant against the Canaanites אשר אנכי יושב בקרבו ('in whose MIDST I dwell,' 24:3)...

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:3 (the pair's second leg)
claim_en: ...and the servant retells it אשר אנכי ישב בארצו ('in whose LAND I dwell,' 24:37) — midst becomes land in the retelling, exactly the Masorah's pair (mnemonic: 'I am YHWH in the midst of the land,' Exod 8:18; edge).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:65 ('הלזה — the heh with PATACH')
claim_en: הלזה ('who is THIS MAN walking in the field toward us?') — heh in patach as ruled, and the word stands exactly TWICE in the Torah: Rebecca's first sight of Isaac (24:65) and the brothers' 'behold, THIS dreamer comes' (37:19) — the this-one word opens on a bridegroom and returns on a betrayal.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 24:65 (the pointing leg)
claim_en: ...the patach verified in the stream.
